headline: Latent Compaction reports retrieval accuracy gains from document-specific test-time KV-cache training
summary: A 14 October arXiv preprint introduces Latent Compaction, which uses test-time training to optimize a compact, document-specific key–value cache while keeping model weights frozen. The authors report a highlighted RULER result of 96.7% accuracy at 32× compression versus 40.0% for KVZip+, and report broader gains on LongBench at stronger compression ratios across Qwen3 model sizes. The paper also states that text summarization outperforms Latent Compaction on RULER at the most aggressive ratios and that Phonebook Lookup accuracy approaches zero for all compressed methods at 64× and above. These are author-reported benchmark results. The evaluation counts logical KV pairs; it does not measure actual memory savings or inference speed.
